corpus_definition: Traveling using a boat or ship.
usage_note: Fixed phrase with no article: 'by sea', not 'by the sea' (that means 'near the sea'). Same pattern: by air, by land, by car.

relations.note: Travelling or sending things by plane.

context.text: My uncle sends carpets to Turkey by sea because it is cheaper. Sending them by sea takes about a month.

reviewer_note: 'by the sea' is a different meaning (location).

particle_note: Separable: 'call me back' or 'call back later'. With a pronoun the object goes in the middle: 'call her back', not 'call back her'.

context.text: Dilnoza was busy in a meeting, so she asked me to call her back. I called back an hour later and we talked.

corpus_definition: to become quiet and less angry or upset
particle_note: Can be used without an object ('Calm down!') or separable with one: 'calm the baby down', 'calm him down'.

context.text: The little boy was crying in the shop. His mother held him and calmed him down, and soon he calmed down completely.

reviewer_note: 'Calm down!' can sound rude to an adult; worth a learner tip.

corpus_definition: A long, narrow passage of water made for boats or irrigation.

forms.definition: a long, narrow waterway made by people for boats or for watering fields
forms.example: The farmers use a canal to water their cotton.

syn.note: Any river or canal that boats use.
A narrow passage of water, natural or made.

context.text: Uzbekistan has many old canals for watering fields. The Great Fergana Canal was built in 1939.

reviewer_note: 'canal' in body sense (ear canal) is a different meaning, not shown.

corpus_definition: Having the skill or power to do something.
usage_note: Followed by a noun or -ing form: 'capable of winning', not 'capable to win'.

relations.note: Same meaning, but followed by the base verb: 'able to win'.
Skilled at something you do often.

context.text: Sardor is capable of running ten kilometres. His coach thinks he is capable of winning the race.

reviewer_note: Main contrast for learners: capable OF + -ing vs able TO + verb.

corpus_definition: The person who is the leader of a sports group.

forms.definition: the leader of a sports team

syn.note: A person who leads a group.

forms.definition: the job of being the leader of a sports team, or the time someone does it
forms.example: Under her captaincy, the team won every game.

syn.note: The act of leading a group.

forms.definition: to be the leader of a sports team
forms.example: He captained the school football team.

syn.note: Be in charge of a group.

people.definition: the person in charge of a ship or plane
people.example: The captain spoke to the passengers.
people.note: Belongs to captain = person in charge of a ship or plane, not a sports leader.

context.text: Aziz is the captain of our volleyball team. He has captained the team for two years, and his captaincy has brought us three cups.

reviewer_note: Ship/plane captain is a different meaning.

corpus_definition: the job or series of jobs you do during your working life

forms.definition: the jobs you do during your working life, usually in one area
forms.example: She wants a career in medicine.

syn.note: A job that needs special training.
One piece of work; a career is many jobs over time.

forms.definition: to move very fast and out of control
forms.example: The car careered off the road.
forms.note: Belongs to career = move fast without control, not working life.
'career' is used before nouns (a career woman), but that is a noun used as a modifier.

context.text: My sister started her career as a teacher in Bukhara. Now her career is in school management.

reviewer_note: Verb career (move fast) is a separate meaning; 'careerist' not shown (rare).

corpus_definition: Not paying enough attention to what you are doing.

forms.definition: attention you give to doing something well and safely

syn.note: Thinking carefully about what you do.

forms.definition: the fact of not paying enough attention
forms.example: The accident happened because of carelessness.
He doesn't care about his marks.

forms.definition: not thinking enough about what you are doing, so you make mistakes
forms.example: I made a careless mistake in my test.

forms.definition: paying attention so that you do not make mistakes

forms.example: He drove carelessly and hit a wall.

context.text: Malika was careless and left her phone on the bus. Next time she will be more careful.

reviewer_note: careful is family (care + -ful), so not listed as antonym.

corpus_definition: a person who looks after a building or place

forms.definition: a person whose job is to look after a building
forms.example: The school caretaker fixed the broken door.

context.text: Our school caretaker opens the gates every morning. Everyone likes the caretaker because he is kind.

reviewer_note: Compound headword from the corpus; no family forms added (rule 7). janitor is American English synonym.

corpus_definition: Not formal or fancy, suitable for everyday wear.

forms.definition: a relaxed, informal way of acting or dressing
forms.example: I like the casualness of the office.

forms.definition: a person hurt or killed in an accident or war
forms.example: There were no casualties in the crash.
forms.note: Belongs to an old sense of casual = by chance, not informal clothes.

forms.definition: relaxed and not formal, for everyday use
forms.example: He wears casual clothes at the weekend.

ant.note: Right for official or serious events.
British English: neat and well dressed.

forms.example: She was dressed casually in jeans.

context.text: On Fridays our office is casual. Most people dress casually in jeans and T-shirts.

reviewer_note: casualty is historically related but a different meaning.
